chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār and Zurārah, from one of them, peace be upon them, who said:

“The woman in nifās refrains from salat (prayer) for the number of days of her menstrual periods during which she used to remain [in menstruation], then she performs ghusl and acts as the mustaḥāḍah acts.”

key_terms.أَيَّامَ أَقْرَائِهَا: the days of her usual menstrual cycles
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the ritual prayer from which she refrains during the specified period
key_terms.النُّفَسَاءُ: a woman in the state of postnatal bleeding
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةُ: a woman experiencing istiḥāḍah whose rulings are then followed
key_terms.تَغْتَسِلُ: she performs ghusl, the ritual bath

ai.seo_question: How long does a woman in nifās leave salat (prayer), and what should she do afterward?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the woman in nifās after childbirth. It states that she leaves salat (prayer) for the duration corresponding to her usual menstrual days, then performs ghusl and thereafter follows the ruling of the mustaḥāḍah.
